tier_reason: The peer-reviewed venue (SC 2025, pp. 695-710, doi 10.1145/3712285.3759876) and the abstract's figures are now confirmed on a page actually opened: the author's publications page in his website repo. The paper body is still blocked (dl.acm.org, theory.stanford.edu), so the CPU model and per-kernel numbers remain unseen and A cannot be assessed. Stays B.

corrections.claimed_speedup: SC 2025 paper abstract (Zhang and Aiken, 'High-Performance Branch-Free Algorithms for Extended-Precision Floating-Point Arithmetic', pp. 695-710, published online 2025-11-15), confirmed on the author's publications page: up to 11.7x the peak performance of QD, 34.4x over CAMPARY, 35.6x over MPFR and 41.4x over FLINT. These are peak-vs-peak figures. The kernel, precision, thread count and CPU behind each peak were not seen, because the paper body could not be opened. The repo commits no result files.

tier_reason: Kept at B on peer review: search results list the paper as ESA 2026, LIPIcs 10.4230/LIPIcs.ESA.2026.22. This listing was seen in two sessions, but the DROPS page itself is egress-blocked. Nothing opened contradicts it, although the rembed README still cites the arXiv preprint. No numbers were verified: the paper is unreachable (arxiv.org, drops.dagstuhl.de) and the repos commit no results.

corrections.claimed_speedup: No speedup numbers verified. The paper (Blaesius, von der Heydt, Kempf, Kobert, Maas, 'Benchmarking and Engineering Data Structures for Spherical Range Queries', arXiv 2607.07367, listed in search results as ESA 2026 LIPIcs) could not be opened, because arxiv.org and drops.dagstuhl.de are blocked. Neither the sprk nor the rembed README quotes results. According to its abstract, seen only in search snippets, the SPRK-tree achieves the fastest query times in almost all benchmarks and ranks second in the rest.
corrections.caveats: Peer review rests on search-result listings of the DROPS/LIPIcs ESA 2026 entry, whose page is blocked. The rembed README's own citation is still the arXiv preprint (@misc). The reproducibility CLI (rembed, reproducability branch) covers Figures 3, 4, 7, 9 and 11 and Tables 2-7, but it needs the Zenodo datasets and commits no results, CPU or compiler. A move to A, or a lower tier, needs the paper.

tier_reason: First-party. The build comparison is inflated by a double nanoflann build in the timed loop (retier-03). An independent benchmark suite that includes PicoTree exists, but its paper (CCGrid 2022 per search results) could not be opened, so its results are unknown and the tier stays C.

corrections.caveats: The 2.6x build ratio is inflated: bm_nanoflann.cpp builds the nanoflann index twice in the timed loop (since nanoflann 1.4 the constructor already calls buildIndex()). The real build gap is about 1.3x (estimate). kNN numbers are unaffected. An independent suite, Lawson/Gropp/Lofstead 'Exploring Spatial Indexing for Accelerated Feature Retrieval in HPC' (arXiv 2106.13972; CCGrid 2022 per search results; code at github.com/mlawsonca/benchmarking_suite_range_searching_libraries, Release build), benchmarks 20 C/C++ libraries including pico_tree (TEST_PICO_TREE) and nanoflann (TEST_NANOFLANN). Its results are only in the paper, which was not opened (arxiv.org, osti.gov and researchgate are blocked), so a retier to B is pending paper access.

tier_reason: Stays C. The FBGEMM paper (arXiv 2101.05615) is a first-party arXiv preprint per the README's own citation, not a peer-reviewed MLSys paper, so it cannot support B. The independent, peer-reviewed Marian WNGT 2019 paper remains unopened.

corrections.caveats: Correction: the FBGEMM paper (Khudia et al., arXiv 2101.05615) is not an MLSys 2021 paper. The README's recommended citation lists it as an 'arXiv preprint' by the FBGEMM team, so it is first-party and would not lift the tier. The independent, peer-reviewed Marian WNGT 2019 paper (ACL D19-5632) remains unopened: aclanthology.org is blocked, the Microsoft Research publication page links only to the ACL Anthology (and its abstract does not mention FBGEMM), and no copy was found on GitHub.
